From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Skyhook-small elevated error surge — initial notice

Hi Samantha —

I wanted to alert you that earlier this morning we observed an elevated rate of 5xx responses and generation timeouts for requests routed to Skyhook-small v2 (your configured model variant). The surge began at ~08:58 PDT and affected a subset of requests with longer context lengths (>1k tokens).

What we're doing now:
- Route new requests to a compatible fallback model (Skyhook-small v1) for your tenant to preserve latency/SLOs.
- Rolling back a recent kernel optimization that appears correlated with the increase (investigation in progress).
- Capturing logs and traces for any requests that failed so we can surface examples to your team.

Immediate impact: some in-flight requests returned 500/timeout; we expect the fallback route to reduce user-visible errors within 10–20 minutes.

I'll keep you updated as we have more concrete root-cause info. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your evaluation workload. If you see anything after this note, please reply and we'll prioritize.

Connor

Subject: Skyhook-small — postmortem summary and credits applied

Samantha —

Final update and summary from our engineering postmortem (attached: skyhook_postmortem.pdf). Key points: 

Root cause:
- A recent optimization to a quantized attention kernel introduced a race condition when handling large KV-cache objects during long-context generation. The issue was exacerbated by a minor GPU driver behavior change between driver versions 510.x -> 512.x on our chosen instance type.

What we did:
- Immediately routed BrightLayer traffic to Skyhook-small v1 (10/30 10:02 PDT) to restore service.
- Rolled back the kernel change and published a stable kernel build after driver-compat checks (10/30 11:30 PDT).
- Executed a controlled canary of the fixed kernel across 10% of capacity on 10/31, then 100% on 11/01 after validation.

Customer impact and remediation:
- Transient failures between 08:58–10:02 PDT on 10/30 affected ~0.6% of BrightLayer's requests (detailed request ids in status_log_excerpt.txt).
- We've applied a service credit worth 2 days of dedicated inference capacity for the affected period; account billing will be adjusted and you'll see the credit applied against invoice BR-2025-1087.

Follow-ups and mitigations to prevent recurrence:
- Hardening: expanded preflight driver compatibility checks in our release pipeline; added an additional integration test that replays long-context KV cache patterns before kernel rollout.
- Observability: added a synthetic long-context generator to our canary harness so regressions with large contexts will surface earlier.
- Playbook: updated runbook with explicit rollback triggers and a faster traffic-splitting path.

Attachments: skyhook_postmortem.pdf (full RCA), status_log_excerpt.txt (sample ids), mitigation_runbook.md

Again, apologies for the disruption. If you'd like a short sync to walk through the postmortem and the fixes, I'm available early next week.

Thanks for partnering with us on this — we appreciate the patience.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
